findings.title: SEEN cache entries for removed Claude accounts are never purged
findings.detail: keychain_has() keeps a static Vec<(Option<PathBuf>, Instant)> of every config_dir it has ever found a Keychain item for. An entry is only replaced (via retain) the next time the *same* config_dir is looked up again; if an account is later removed (DELETE /v1/accounts/{id}), its config_dir is never queried again, so its entry is never evicted. Since every macOS Claude sign-in writes the login into a Keychain item scoped to the account's own config_dir (docs/runner-api.md: "the login goes to that folder's Keychain item"), an owner who repeatedly adds, signs in and removes Claude accounts over the life of a long-running obid process will grow this Vec without bound. It's a slow leak, but it is unbounded and was introduced by this change (the previous code had no such cache).

findings.title: No regression test for the de-duplicated Keychain lookup
findings.detail: The stated goal is that GET /v1/status no longer asks `security` twice per Claude account within one status call. The Cursor side already has a test (tests/accounts_api.rs, a_cursor_login_only_in_the_keychain_is_found) that counts `security` invocations recorded in obid-test-security-calls to prove the once-a-minute value cache works, but no equivalent test counts `find-generic-password` (non `-w`) calls for the Claude path added here, so a future regression that re-introduces the double ask (or breaks the cache keying) would go unnoticed by the test suite.
